mixing-L02.key_details: IWA Water Supply 2001 article opens through the proxy, but the full text is PDF-only (no HTML full text) and the PDF could not be text-extracted in the browser session. Record unchanged.

updates.scale: Lake Nieuwe Meer, Amsterdam (1.3 km2, mean depth 18 m, max depth 30 m, hypertrophic); 3 sampling stations
updates.dose: Air bubbling from seven perforated air tubes laid just above the sediment (running since 1993); turbulent diffusivity measured with SCAMP microstructure profiler
updates.duration: Mixing switched off 19 July - 7 August 2002 and back on, turbulence measured under both regimes; model simulations
updates.result: Mean turbulent diffusivity was 0.17 cm2/s with mixing off and 5.1 cm2/s with mixing on (t test P < 0.0001); the model puts the Microcystis-vs-diatoms/greens switch at D of about 3.4 cm2/s, so artificial mixing moves the lake into the diatom/green-dominated regime. The observed replacement of Microcystis by diatoms and greens is cited from earlier work (Visser et al. 1996a), not new counts.

mixing-L03.key_details: Huisman et al. 2004 parameterised a light-competition model for Microcystis versus lumped diatoms and greens in Lake Nieuwe Meer. Mixing was switched off for about 3 weeks in July-August 2002: the lake stratified within 10 days (thermocline ~5 m) and phytoplankton concentrated in the top 2.5 m. Diffusivity averaged 0.17 cm2/s (N = 105) off vs 5.1 cm2/s (N = 110) on. The model predicts Microcystis surface blooms above 5 x 10^6 cells/mL under weak mixing and diatom/green dominance under intense mixing, with the boundary at D of about 3.4 cm2/s for 18 m depth. No new Microcystis biomass reduction figure is given; it is a mechanism and model-validation paper.
mixing-L03.discrepancy: Record says 'multi-year lake experiment'; the new field work is a ~3-week mixing switch-off in summer 2002 plus modelling. The species shift itself is taken from earlier Nieuwe Meer studies.

updates.scale: Tegeler See, Berlin (4 km2, max depth 16 m, mean depth 6 m); 15 Limnox hypolimnetic aerators at 12-16 m depth (installed 1980)
updates.dose: Continuous summer aeration (1989, 1990), no aeration (1992), surge aeration events after stable stratification (1993, 1994); mixing tracked with the Lake number
updates.result: Continuous aeration did not affect Microcystis population dynamics in 1989 and 1990, even with Lake numbers below 1, and favoured Microcystis over Ceratium. Surge aeration events in 1993 and 1994 were each followed by a Microcystis decline and delayed its growth, although a stock persisted into September; no percentage reduction is given.
updates.env_effects: Surge aeration had no noticeable effect on the distribution of total inorganic nitrogen or total phosphorus. TP was also falling year on year from external remediation (>50 ug/L in 1989-92 to 30-40 ug/L in 1994), a confounder. Continuous aeration suppressed Ceratium.

mixing-L04.key_details: Single-lake, multi-year observational comparison of aerator operating schemes, with no control lake and no replication within years. Evidence is qualitative from time series of Microcystis and Ceratium biomass against Lake number (figure only, no tabulated numbers). Microcystis formed very large colonies (up to tennis-ball size) and adapted to continuous mixing. The author concludes surge aeration after prolonged stability hinders slow-growing Microcystis, while continuous aeration strengthens it against Ceratium. Declining phosphorus over 1993-94 confounds the surge-year comparison.
mixing-L04.discrepancy: Record implies a clean 3-scheme test; in fact the aerated years were 1989-90, non-aerated 1992 and surge 1993-94, while TP fell over the same period, so the surge effect is confounded and unquantified.

updates.scale: North Pine Dam (Lake Samsonvale), Brisbane: volume 2x10^8 m3, surface area 19.7 km2, supplies ~30% of Brisbane's water
updates.dose: Bubble-plume destratifier installed 1995: compressor pumping 200 L/s of air through a 90 mm pipe with 33 hole clusters ~17 m apart; runs mid-September to end of April
updates.duration: Phytoplankton record from 1983 (weekly to 1998, then fortnightly); temperature/DO compared 1978-94 vs 1998-2002; chlorophyll trends 1984-2002
updates.result: After destratification most taxa increased significantly at the dam wall: Cylindrospermopsis rose from 5584 to 9372 cells/mL and Microcystis from 313 to 1829 cells/mL (randomised intervention analysis, P < 0.025). Only the rate of eutrophication slowed: the chlorophyll a increase fell from 0.74 to 0.49 ug/L per year (~30%).
updates.env_effects: Thermocline gradient fell from 1 to 0.2 degC/m; the low-DO (<1 mg/L) period shrank from 7 to 3 months and its vertical extent from 15 to <2 m above the bottom. The destratifier's horizontal influence was limited, and upstream sites stayed more stratified.

mixing-L05.key_details: Before-after design at one reservoir with no control reservoir; intervention effects tested by randomised intervention analysis on surface cell counts (sample sizes about 77-507 before and 46-220 after per genus). Significant increases after destratification for cyanobacteria (Anabaena, Cylindrospermopsis, Microcystis, Planktolyngbya, Pseudanabaena), several chlorophytes and diatoms. Chlorophyll a kept rising, but more slowly (0.74 to 0.49 ug/L per year for the full record). Sampling methods changed after 1997, and retention time varies from 1 month to 3 years, which confounds before-after comparisons.
mixing-L05.discrepancy: Record correctly flags a negative result but gives no numbers; the full text shows the dominant toxic cyanobacteria increased (Cylindrospermopsis +68%, Microcystis ~5.8x in mean cells/mL), so effect_pct should be negative (-68 for Cylindrospermopsis).

updates.organism: Field: mixed reservoir phytoplankton dominated by Bacillariophyta and Chlorophyta (cyanobacteria at most 7.58% relative abundance); lab: Microcystis aeruginosa
updates.dose: Eight water-lifting aerators at full load, ~30 m3/h air each, 24 h/day; lab analogue: 6 or 25 degC, light or dark
updates.duration: Field: operated 29 July - 12 October 2019, sampled 28 July, 25 August and 17 October; lab: 72 h (sampled 0-72 h)
updates.result: Surface algal density fell by more than 90% during aerator operation and kept falling after shutdown, with chlorophyll a and photosynthetic yield (mean Fv/Fm 0.435 to 0.074) also falling. In the lab, M. aeruginosa declined only under 6 degC dark (max drop 1.04 x 10^5 cells/mL, 37.08 ug/L chl a).
updates.env_effects: Lower surface water temperature, more uniform vertical profiles of algae, temperature, pH and DO. The cyanobacteria share rose slightly after operation (max 7.58% at 30 m).

mixing-L09.key_details: Field study at Lijiahe Reservoir (Xi'an, China) with one before, one during and one after sampling date at 7 depths (0-bottom), triplicate analyses (n = 3), and no control reservoir or site. The '>90%' surface density decrease is confounded by season (July to October) and by mixing moving cells to depth rather than removing them. The lab arm simulated surface (25 degC light) vs bottom (6 degC dark) conditions for M. aeruginosa; growth stopped and cells, dehydrogenase, ATP and photosynthesis fell under cold dark conditions. The reservoir community was mostly diatoms and green algae, not Microcystis.
mixing-L09.discrepancy: Record implies a Microcystis bloom was controlled in the field; the field phytoplankton was diatom/green dominated (cyanobacteria <=7.58%) and Microcystis was only a lab culture. The full text gives a >90% surface density reduction (unreplicated, seasonally confounded); lab cultures ran 72 h, not 48 h.
